name: Vitamin D (Cholecalciferol)
summary: A fat-soluble secosteroid that regulates intestinal calcium and phosphate absorption and bone mineralisation. Synthesised in skin on UVB exposure and obtained from diet.

conditions.label: Deficiency
conditions.description: Low vitamin D impairs calcium/phosphate homeostasis, causing defective bone mineralisation and secondary hyperparathyroidism.

affects.detail: Inadequate calcium-phosphate deposition softens the bone matrix (osteoid). Weight-bearing bones deform and fracture risk rises.

ageModifiers.infant: Growth-plate widening, craniotabes (soft skull), delayed fontanelle closure and bowing of the legs as weight-bearing begins.
ageModifiers.child: Rickets: bowed legs or knock-knees, widened wrists, rachitic rosary at the costochondral junctions and delayed growth.
ageModifiers.adolescent: Bone pain and reduced peak bone mass accrual during the growth spurt.
ageModifiers.adult: Osteomalacia: diffuse bone pain, proximal muscle weakness and pseudofractures (Looser zones).
ageModifiers.elderly: Accelerated osteoporosis and markedly higher risk of hip and vertebral fractures.

affects.detail: Low vitamin D status is linked to proximal myopathy, impaired contractility, a waddling gait and increased falls.

ageModifiers.elderly: Weakness compounds fall and fracture risk; supplementation can reduce falls in deficient older adults.

affects.detail: Impaired mineralisation can affect enamel formation and delay tooth eruption in children.

conditions.label: Toxicity (hypervitaminosis D)
conditions.description: Excess vitamin D (almost always from over-supplementation) drives hypercalcaemia.

affects.detail: Sustained hypercalcaemia causes calcium deposition in renal tissue, polyuria, dehydration and acute kidney injury.
Elevated serum calcium shortens the QT interval and can provoke arrhythmias.
Hypercalcaemia depresses the central nervous system, producing lethargy, confusion and in severe cases stupor.
